formats.key: exactInput((bytes path, address recipient, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMinimum) params)
effects: The signer sends exactly amountIn of the first token in path; the router pulls it with transferFrom, or wraps the signer's ETH when the first token is WETH9 and ETH was sent.
The recipient receives at least amountOutMinimum of the last token in path; the call reverts below that.
Recipient 0x...01 means the signer; recipient 0x...02 means the router keeps the output, and anyone can then sweep it.
amountIn = 0 swaps the router's own balance of the first token instead of pulling from the signer.
ETH sent with the call and not used for the swap stays in the router; this call does not refund it.
formats.shown: "Swap", with the amount sent in the first path token, the minimum received in the last path token, and the beneficiary address.

findings.title: exactInput is payable but no field shows the native ETH sent with the call.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactInput is `external payable`; PeripheryPayments.pay: `if (token == WETH9 && address(this).balance >= value) { IWETH9(WETH9).deposit{value: value}(); ...}`. The descriptor's exactInput fields have no `@.value` field.

findings.title: exactInput shows the recipient flags 0x...01 (signer) and 0x...02 (router) as raw addresses.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactInputInternal: `if (recipient == Constants.MSG_SENDER) recipient = msg.sender; else if (recipient == Constants.ADDRESS_THIS) recipient = address(this);`. The Beneficiary field has no `senderAddress`.
findings.fix: Add "senderAddress": ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001"] to the Beneficiary field params. Also make 0x...02 visibly mean the router.

findings.title: exactInput shows amountIn 0 as '0', but the code then swaps the router's whole balance.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactInput: `if (params.amountIn == Constants.CONTRACT_BALANCE) { hasAlreadyPaid = true; params.amountIn = IERC20(tokenIn).balanceOf(address(this)); }`, with CONTRACT_BALANCE = 0.
findings.fix: Show a message such as "Router balance" when amountIn is 0.

cases.notes: SABAI out 1020.349 and WETH in 0.000905 (minimum 0.000903) both match the screen.

formats.key: exactInputSingle((address tokenIn, address tokenOut, uint24 fee, address recipient, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMinimum, uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96) params)
effects: The signer sends up to amountIn of tokenIn, pulled with transferFrom, or wrapped from sent ETH when tokenIn is WETH9.
The recipient receives at least amountOutMinimum of tokenOut from the fee-tier pool.
A non-zero sqrtPriceLimitX96 can stop the swap early, so less than amountIn leaves.
Recipient 0x...01 means the signer; 0x...02 means the router keeps the output.
amountIn = 0 swaps the router's own balance of tokenIn.
ETH sent and not used stays in the router.
formats.shown: "swap", with the amount sent in tokenIn, the minimum received in tokenOut, the pool fee tier as a percent, and the beneficiary.

findings.title: exactInputSingle is payable but no field shows the native ETH sent with the call.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactInputSingle is `external payable`; PeripheryPayments.pay wraps router ETH when token == WETH9. The descriptor's exactInputSingle fields have no `@.value` field.

findings.title: exactInputSingle shows the recipient flags 0x...01 and 0x...02 as raw addresses.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactInputInternal maps Constants.MSG_SENDER to msg.sender and Constants.ADDRESS_THIS to address(this). The Beneficiary field has no `senderAddress`.
findings.fix: Add "senderAddress": ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001"] to the Beneficiary field params.

findings.title: exactInputSingle shows amountIn 0 literally, but the code then swaps the router's whole balance.
findings.fix: Show a message such as "Router balance" when amountIn is 0.

findings.title: exactInputSingle hides sqrtPriceLimitX96, which can make less than the 'Send' amount leave.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactInputInternal passes `sqrtPriceLimitX96` to pool.swap; the descriptor has no field for params.sqrtPriceLimitX96.
findings.fix: Label the amount "Send (up to)" or add the price limit as a field.

findings.title: exactInputSingle intent is lowercase 'swap', unlike its sibling formats.
findings.evidence: descriptor exactInputSingle: "intent": "swap"; the other formats use "Swap".

cases.notes: WETH out 0.006471 and USDT in 13.97 (minimum 13.90) match the screen.

formats.key: exactOutput((bytes path, address recipient, uint256 amountOut, uint256 amountInMaximum) params)

The signer pays at most amountInMaximum of the last token in the path, pulled with transferFrom, or wrapped from sent ETH when it is WETH9.
Recipient 0x...01 means the signer; 0x...02 means the router keeps the output.
ETH sent and not used stays in the router; this call does not refund it.
formats.shown: "Swap", with the maximum paid in the input token, the exact amount received in the output token, and the beneficiary.

findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactOutputInternal: `if (recipient == Constants.MSG_SENDER) recipient = msg.sender; else if (recipient == Constants.ADDRESS_THIS) recipient = address(this);`. The Beneficiary field has no `senderAddress`.

cases.notes: SABAI in 2636.309 exact and WETH out 0.0023536 under the 0.0023606 maximum both match.

effects: The recipient receives amountOut of tokenOut; when sqrtPriceLimitX96 is non-zero the exact-output check is skipped, so less can arrive.
The signer pays at most amountInMaximum of tokenIn, pulled with transferFrom, or wrapped from sent ETH when tokenIn is WETH9.
Recipient 0x...01 means the signer; 0x...02 means the router keeps the output.
ETH sent and not used stays in the router.
formats.shown: "Swap", with the maximum paid in tokenIn, the amount received in tokenOut, the pool fee tier, and the beneficiary.

findings.title: exactOutputSingle is payable but no field shows the native ETH sent with the call.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactOutputSingle is `external payable`; PeripheryPayments.pay wraps router ETH when token == WETH9. The descriptor's exactOutputSingle fields have no `@.value` field.

findings.title: exactOutputSingle hides sqrtPriceLimitX96; a non-zero limit lets less than 'Amount to Receive' arrive.
findings.evidence: V3SwapRouter.exactOutputInternal: `if (sqrtPriceLimitX96 == 0) require(amountOutReceived == amountOut);`. The descriptor has no field for params.sqrtPriceLimitX96.
findings.fix: Add a field for params.sqrtPriceLimitX96 (raw, labeled "Price limit (0 = none)"), or label the amount "Receive (up to)".

formats.key: swapExactTokensForTokens(uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMin, address[] path, address to)
effects: The signer sends amountIn of path[0] to the first V2 pair, pulled with transferFrom, or wrapped from sent ETH when path[0] is WETH9.
The recipient receives at least amountOutMin of path[-1], measured as the recipient's balance change.
Recipient 0x...01 means the signer; 0x...02 means the router keeps the output.
amountIn = 0 swaps the router's own balance of path[0].
ETH sent and not used stays in the router.
formats.shown: "Swap", with the amount sent in path[0], the minimum received in path[-1], and the recipient.

findings.title: swapExactTokensForTokens is payable but no field shows the native ETH sent with the call.
findings.evidence: V2SwapRouter.swapExactTokensForTokens is `external payable` and calls `pay(path[0], ...)`, which wraps router ETH when the token is WETH9. The descriptor has no `@.value` field.

findings.title: swapExactTokensForTokens shows the recipient flags 0x...01 and 0x...02 as raw addresses.
findings.evidence: V2SwapRouter.swapExactTokensForTokens: `if (to == Constants.MSG_SENDER) to = msg.sender; else if (to == Constants.ADDRESS_THIS) to = address(this);`. The Recipient field has no `senderAddress`.
findings.fix: Add "senderAddress": ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001"] to the Recipient field params.

findings.title: swapExactTokensForTokens shows amountIn 0 literally, but the code then swaps the router's balance.
findings.evidence: V2SwapRouter.swapExactTokensForTokens: `if (amountIn == Constants.CONTRACT_BALANCE) { hasAlreadyPaid = true; amountIn = IERC20(path[0]).balanceOf(address(this)); }`.
findings.fix: Show a message such as "Router balance" when amountIn is 0.

cases.notes: Synthetic. Tokens and amounts render correctly from the code.

formats.key: swapTokensForExactTokens(uint256 amountOut, uint256 amountInMax, address[] path, address to)
effects: The recipient receives amountOut of path[-1] through V2 pairs.
The signer pays the computed amountIn, at most amountInMax, of path[0], pulled with transferFrom, or wrapped from sent ETH when path[0] is WETH9.
Recipient 0x...01 means the signer; 0x...02 means the router keeps the output.
ETH sent and not used stays in the router.
formats.shown: "Swap", with the amount received in path[-1], the maximum sent in path[0] (Unlimited above 2^255), and the recipient, with 0x...01 shown as the sender.

findings.title: swapTokensForExactTokens is payable but no field shows the native ETH sent with the call.
findings.evidence: V2SwapRouter.swapTokensForExactTokens is `external payable` and calls `pay(path[0], msg.sender, ...)`, which wraps router ETH when the token is WETH9. The descriptor has no `@.value` field.

findings.title: swapTokensForExactTokens shows recipient 0x...02 (the router keeps the output) as a raw address.
findings.evidence: V2SwapRouter.swapTokensForExactTokens: `else if (to == Constants.ADDRESS_THIS) to = address(this);`. The Recipient field maps only 0x...01 through `senderAddress`.
findings.fix: Make 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000002 render as the router, for example through a local address name.
